events.title: Hurricane Katrina strikes
events.description: The hurricane devastates Gulf Coast communities and creates an enormous need for rescue and recovery.

events.title: Apple announces the iPhone
events.description: The company presents a touchscreen device combining a phone, music player and internet functions.

events.title: Bear Stearns faces a rescue deal
events.description: The Federal Reserve approves financing for a deal involving the troubled investment bank and JPMorgan Chase.

what_happened_next.text:
The international share basket nearly tripled, leading this set. Costco ended about $2.25 per starting dollar and Intel about $1.39, while Merck ended near 88 cents. Intel gained less than the broad U.S. share basket. The hopeful investment ideas available in March 2003 were opinions to examine, not instructions guaranteed to work.

Costco reported $64.4 billion in fiscal-2007 revenue and 6% comparable-sales growth. Intel reported that 2007 revenue rose 8% and operating income 45% as customers embraced its Core design. Merck’s Vioxx medicine had brought in $2.5 billion in 2003 sales before the company withdrew it worldwide in September 2004, expecting an earnings hit. Business news helps us understand what changed, but does not create a simple stock formula.

The years ahead included Hurricane Katrina, Apple’s iPhone announcement and a rescue deal involving Bear Stearns in March 2008. This window ends that month. Later stages of the financial crisis do not belong in the five-year result, even though a reader today may know what followed. A dividend or a strong business cannot shield a share from every loss.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: The Iraq invasion dominated attention. Some economists hoped less uncertainty would lift spending, while daily life and new products continued.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The risks of each company still mattered. Even a medicine maker paying dividends could lose value for its shareholders. The international share basket followed a different path.
reflection.what_faded_away: A confident wartime forecast did not tell you which investment would lead. Calling a stock a safe haven did not remove its risks.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: Nobody knew the coming company surprises or financial stress. This window ends in March 2008, so later events are outside its return chart.

hot:2003-03:costco.text: Costco reported $64.4 billion in fiscal 2007 revenue and 6% growth in comparable sales. Comparable sales count changes at warehouses open at least a year, showing that existing stores were attracting more shopping as Costco kept expanding its warehouse business.

hot:2003-03:intel.text: Intel introduced its Core Duo processor for laptops in January 2006, bringing strong computing performance to mobile computers. In 2007, revenue rose 8% and operating income rose 45%; Intel said customers were responding to its Core chip designs.

hot:2003-03:merck.text: Merck withdrew Vioxx worldwide on September 30, 2004, after safety concerns. The medicine had brought in $2.5 billion in 2003 sales, and Merck expected its removal to reduce earnings. Losing a major drug meant less sales and more pressure on the company’s profits.
